Create a production-style iOS mobile app prototype from this design reference: Figma Make reference. Use the reference for layout direction and iOS visual language, but build a complete, fully functional app experience rather than a static mockup.

Use the image below

![][image1]

**Role**  
Act as a senior iOS product designer, mobile UX designer, and full-stack app builder. Design and generate a polished iPhone-first app with realistic flows, connected screens, reusable components, clean information architecture, and functional state logic.

**Build Goal**  
Create a complete iOS app, not just UI screens. The output must feel like a launch-ready MVP with end-to-end user journeys, interactive navigation, form validation, empty states, loading states, success states, error handling, and realistic sample data.

**Product Definition**  
If the Figma reference does not clearly define the product type, infer a coherent app concept from the screen patterns and keep it consistent across the full build. Do not ask follow-up questions. Choose one strong app idea and complete it fully.  
**Platform and Constraints**  
	•	Target platform: iOS only, optimized for iPhone 15/16 viewport first.  
	•	Use native iOS design patterns inspired by Apple Human Interface style: safe areas, bottom tab bar, navigation stacks, cards, sheets, segmented controls, search, swipe actions, toggles, and haptic-friendly interactions.  
	•	Use mobile-first responsive behavior for smaller and larger iPhone sizes.  
	•	Support light mode and dark mode.  
	•	Ensure accessibility: readable contrast, scalable text behavior, clear **focus/selection states, and tappable targets.**  
**Core Deliverable**  
Build the full app with these connected parts:  
	1\.	Onboarding and permission flow.  
	2\.	Authentication flow: sign up, log in, forgot password, OTP or verification state.  
	3\.	Main app shell with tab navigation.  
	4\.	Home/dashboard screen.  
	5\.	Browse/discover or primary task flow.  
	6\.	Detail screen for an item/entity.  
	7\.	Create/edit flow with forms.  
	8\.	Search and filter experience.  
	9\.	Saved/favorites/history area.  
	10\.	Profile/settings/account area.  
	11\.	Notifications/inbox or activity feed.  
	12\.	Empty, loading, success, offline, and error states.  
**Required Screens**  
**Generate at minimum these screens and connect them logically:**  
	•	Splash  
	•	Onboarding  
	•	Welcome/Auth choice  
	•	Login  
	•	Sign up  
	•	Forgot password  
	•	Home  
	•	Search/Explore  
	•	Item list or feed  
	•	Item detail  
	•	Create/Edit form  
	•	Saved/Favorites  
	•	Notifications  
	•	Profile  
	•	Settings  
	•	Success state modal/sheet  
	•	Error/empty state screen  
**Functional Requirements**  
**Make the prototype genuinely interactive:**  
	•	Bottom tabs must switch between major sections.  
	•	Cards and list items must open detail pages.  
	•	Search must filter local sample data.  
	•	Filters/sort must update visible results.  
	•	Forms must include validation, required fields, disabled/enabled button states, **inline errors, and submit confirmation.**  
	•	Save/favorite actions must toggle state.  
	•	Settings must include working toggles and selection controls.  
	•	Notifications or activity items must have read/unread behavior.  
	•	Use realistic mock data across all screens.  
	•	Preserve state during navigation within the prototype where possible.  
**UX Quality Bar**  
**Design like a strong App Store MVP:**  
	•	Clear hierarchy and one primary action per screen.  
	•	Consistent spacing, typography, iconography, and component system.  
	•	Native-feeling transitions, sheets, sticky headers where helpful, and **bottom-safe-area treatment.**  
	•	Use skeleton loaders or subtle loading placeholders.  
	•	Include helpful empty states with guidance.  
	•	Avoid generic AI-looking gradients or random decoration.  
	**•	Keep visuals premium, minimal, and practical.**  
**Visual System**  
**Use an iOS-native aesthetic:**  
	•	Clean white/light surfaces and elegant dark mode.  
	•	Rounded cards and controls with restrained shadows.  
	•	San Francisco-style system typography or closest native equivalent.  
	•	Accent color used intentionally, not everywhere.  
	•	Use SF Symbols-style icons or close equivalents.  
	•	Follow an 8pt spacing system.  
**Information Architecture**  
**Structure the app with this pattern unless the Figma strongly suggests better:**  
	•	Tab 1: Home  
	•	Tab 2: Explore/Search  
	•	Tab 3: Create or Primary Action  
	•	Tab 4: Saved/Activity  
	•	Tab 5: Profile  
**Use drill-down navigation for detail pages and modal sheets for quick actions, filters, confirmations, and edits.**  
**Content Rules**  
	•	Use realistic names, labels, helper text, and microcopy.  
	•	Avoid lorem ipsum.  
	•	Write concise product-quality UX copy.  
	•	Keep terminology consistent across all screens.  
	•	Include at least 8–12 realistic sample records/items for lists.  
**Components to Create**  
**Build reusable components and use them consistently:**  
	•	Top navigation bars  
	•	Bottom tab bar  
	•	Search bar  
	•	Segmented controls  
	•	Cards  
	•	List cells  
	•	Buttons: primary, secondary, destructive, ghost  
	•	Input fields, text areas, dropdown/select, toggle, checkbox/radio if needed  
	•	Filter chips  
	•	Empty state blocks  
	•	Toast/snackbar or confirmation feedback  
	•	Modal sheet / bottom sheet  
	•	Profile row items  
**State Design**  
**Every key screen should account for:**  
	•	Default state  
	•	Loading state  
	•	Empty state  
	•	Error state  
	•	Success state  
	•	Populated state  
	•	First-time user guidance where relevant  
**Data Model**  
Infer a lightweight but coherent data model for the chosen app concept. Include entities, attributes, relationships, and mock records sufficient to power lists, details, search, saves, notifications, and profile activity.  
Build Output Expectations  
Generate:  
	•	Complete app structure and navigation  
	•	Fully designed screens  
	•	Interactive prototype logic  
	•	Reusable design system/components  
	•	Realistic mock data  
	•	Clean naming and organized files/code structure  
**Final Instruction**  
Do not return a partial concept. Return a complete iOS app build with all major screens, connected user flows, functional prototype interactions, and polished production-level mobile UX based on the linked Figma direction.
